authority_status.xsd_boundary: No dedicated HDS service XSD is selected or inferred.

HDS_V2.2.fresh_read_rule: Independently derive V2.2 behavior from the pinned V2.2 source before reconciling historical V2.2 profile notes.
HDS_V2.2.historical_context_note: The broader historical HDS block had already been seen during the prior V2.1 reconciliation. For this V2.2 pass, no historical V2.2 statement was used as factual authority: all V2.2 observations below were independently re-derived from the pinned V2.2 bytes before V2.2 reconciliation.
fresh_observations: The publication again states that HtmlDisplayService defines no own protocol and uses DNS-SD plus HTTP/browser delivery.
V2.2 publishes service name HtmlDisplayService over _http._tcp.
The V2.2 TXT record contains content and url.
TXT url contains the access URL and may also contain query or fragment components.
TXT content remains project-specific and not standardized by the publication.
Multiple URLs require separate DNS-SD entries with corresponding content names.
SRV port is still published but explicitly has no meaning for the content access address; SRV host identifies the publishing device.
The publication imposes no HTTP-content requirements beyond browser/provider interoperability being agreed between suppliers.
The V2.2 version history explicitly records new TXT url replacing host, port and path for access-address construction.
The official VDV-301-2.2 tag contains no dedicated HtmlDisplayService service XSD.
active_falsification: Potential contradiction rejected: version-history wording that url replaces host/port/path does not mean SRV host/port records disappear; the main profile still lists them and assigns publisher/discovery-only roles.
Potential hidden-XSD inference rejected: foreword wording about specific data structures is insufficient to establish an XML contract, and no dedicated HDS schema exists in the exact official tag.
